ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Pacifying the mind and severing the arm is the compact Huike–Bodhidharma case label that joins the demand to bring forth the mind with the severed-arm episode.
EvidenceBody: Gulin lists “pacifying the mind and severing the arm” among demanding precedents that can make later students retreat. Other records use the compact phrase in verses or teaching titles, and only the Gulin witness supplies the stored critical deployment. The entry therefore names the later case label; it does not certify the biography or assign every citation to Gulin.
